summary_rationale: Proventus Agrocom has shown real operating momentum: brand revenue grew 58% in FY2026 and 61% in H1 FY27, volume and pouch counts are rising, reported gross margin improved from 7.2% in FY2023 to 12.0% in H1 FY27, other income has faded as a share of earnings, and consolidated profit has grown every year since the shift away from bulk commodity trading. Against that, the audited base is still a roughly 2% EBITDA-margin trading business, about 85% of each gross-margin gain has been reinvested in marketing, staff and distribution, cumulative operating cash flow for FY2023 to FY2026 was about ₹0.7 crore against ₹32.5 crore of profit, and H1 FY27 operating cash flow was −₹57.6 crore with net cash of ₹19.6 crore turning into net debt of about ₹51 crore. Our estimate is that the business can fund only about 14% growth a year from its own cash earnings, well below the guide. Management beat its revenue promises but missed Surat dates, the FY2025 EBITDA guide and its no-cash-burn pledge, its brand gross margin and marketing figures cannot be reconciled to the filed statements, ROCE is near 12%, the board has two independent directors, and the statutory auditor resigned mid-term. The evidence supports a credible, growing brand with unproven cash compounding, so the call remains conditional on a full year of positive operating cash flow, disclosed repeat and segment economics, and Surat utilisation.
